messages.content:
You are an expert power-electronics designer synthesising the interface circuit of a
piezoelectric energy harvester. You work by experiment: you propose a circuit, it is simulated in
LTspice under several operating conditions, and you receive the measurements.

GOAL
A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node "out".
Under EVERY operating condition below, starting from 0 V (cold start) and simulating 0.8 s:
  vout_min: vavg >= 1.8 V (settled mean output reaches the load's minimum supply)
  vout_max: vmax <= 3.6 V (output never exceeds the load's absolute maximum)
  ripple: vpp <= 0.05 V (peak-to-peak ripple in the final window)
  startup: tup <= 0.4 s (cold start: first time output reaches 1.8 V)
  settled: dv <= 0.02 V (mean output changes little between the last two windows)
Measurement windows: vavg and vpp over 0.7-0.8 s; vmax over the whole run; tup = first time
V(out) reaches 1.8 V (missing if never); dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)|.

PIEZO MODEL AND OPERATING CONDITIONS
The piezo is a sinusoidal current source Ip*sin(2*pi*f*t) in parallel with its capacitance Cp and a
20 MOhm leakage resistance, between nodes pzp and pzn (Cp = 25 nF nominal).
Its open-circuit voltage amplitude is Ip/(2*pi*f*Cp), about 3.2 V at nominal: low, so diode drops matter.
  S1: nominal; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S2: heavy load; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 150 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S3: strong excitation, light load; Ip = 100 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 2200 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S4: weak excitation; Ip = 30 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 1000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S5: low frequency; Ip = 40 uA peak, f = 80 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 470 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S6: Cp +20 %, hot; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 30 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 60 C

TEST BENCH (fixed, added automatically - do not include these)
- the piezo model between pzp and pzn; the load RL from out to 0;
- for every SYNC controller you use, a 0.5 uA supply current drawn from out (its power cost);
- a 1 GOhm resistor to 0 from pzp, pzn and every internal node (prevents floating nodes).

COMPONENTS YOU MAY USE (at most 16 components)
- R  resistor, value 1..1e+08 Ohm, nodes [a, b]
- C  capacitor, value 1e-10..4.7e-05 F, nodes [a, b]
- L  inductor, value 1e-05..0.01 H; it has series resistance 2 Ohm + 5 Ohm per mH
- D  diode, nodes [anode, cathode]: forward current flows from the first node to the second.
     Model one of DSCH, DSI, DZ33:
     DSCH = low-drop Schottky (~0.25 V at uA), DSI = silicon small-signal (~0.5 V at uA),
     DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)
     Orientation matters:
       full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have
       their anode on ground);
       zener clamp on out: ["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at
       3.3 V). ["out", "0"] would be forward-biased and hold out near 0.7 V; it is rejected.
- S  switch, nodes [a, b], "ctrl": id of a SYNC; Ron = 2 Ohm, Roff = 1 GOhm (at most 4)
- SYNC ideal synchronous controller (no nodes, at most 2): closes its switches for "ton"
     seconds (1e-07..0.001) at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero
     crossings of the piezo current. "edges": "both" (every half period), "pos" (positive peak only)
     or "neg" (negative peak only). "phase" shifts the pulses by that fraction of the excitation
     period (-0.25..0.25). It tracks the excitation frequency automatically.
     For L-Cp inversion, ton is about pi*sqrt(L*Cp).
Nodes: "0" is ground; pzp, pzn are the piezo terminals; out is the load/storage node; name any other
nodes yourself (lower-case, e.g. n1, mid). Every node needs at least two connections, and out must
connect to the piezo through your circuit.

REFERENCE DESIGN: FBR (full-bridge rectifier, 4 x DSCH, 2.2 uF on out). Its results:
cond   vavg V  vmax V  vpp mV   tup s  Pload uW  vout_min vout_max ripple   startup  settled 
S1       2.24    2.25    26.2   0.269      15.2  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S2       1.76    1.77    20.3       -      20.7  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     ok      
S3       5.68    5.72    84.4  0.0779      14.7  ok       FAIL     FAIL     ok       FAIL    
S4       1.51    1.52    20.8       -      2.27  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL    
S5       2.26    2.28    43.5   0.318      10.9  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S6       1.93    1.94    18.8   0.379      11.3  ok       ok       ok       ok       ok      

HOW TO WORK
- Component values are optimised automatically (an evolution strategy, up to 48 full
  evaluations per structure, running while you think), so spend your reasoning on circuit
  CONNECTIVITY (topology): which structure can meet every condition. A structure that was already
  explored is not simulated again, whatever its values.
- Each proposal is first SCREENED: with out fixed at 1.8 V, the net power it delivers is
  measured on S2, S4, S6 for its proposed values and a few automatic value presets.
  If the best preset delivers less than 50 % of the load's need (V^2/RL) on any of them,
  the design is reported back with those powers and is not tuned or simulated further.
- Each round, propose up to 3 designs with DIFFERENT connectivity (different structures, not value variants).
- Classify each design with "move": new_topology or modify_topology, and explain the expected effect
  in "rationale". Set "done": true only when you believe no further structural change can improve on
  the best design so far.
- Reply with ONE JSON object only, in this form:
{
 "proposals": [
  {
   "move": "new_topology",
   "name": "short label for this design",
   "rationale": "what you changed and why it should fix the failing checks",
   "done": false,
   "components": [
    {
     "id": "D1",
     "type": "D",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "out"
     ],
     "model": "DSCH"
    },
    {
     "id": "C1",
     "type": "C",
     "nodes": [
      "out",
      "0"
     ],
     "value": 2.2e-06
    },
    {
     "id": "L1",
     "type": "L",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "n1"
     ],
     "value": 0.0047
    },
    {
     "id": "S1",
     "type": "S",
     "nodes": [
      "n1",
      "pzn"
     ],
     "ctrl": "G1"
    },
    {
     "id": "G1",
     "type": "SYNC",
     "ton": 3.4e-05,
     "phase": 0.0,
     "edges": "both"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}

Round 1 of 12.

This is your first round: choose the structures you think most likely to meet every condition.

Reply with one JSON object only.

reply.reasoning:
*   Input: Piezoelectric energy harvester (sinusoidal current source $I_p \sin(2\pi ft)$ in parallel with $C_p$ and $R_{leak} = 20 \text{ M}\Omega$).
    *   Output: Power a sensor node $R_L$ from a storage capacitor $C_{out}$ at node "out".
    *   Requirements:
        *   $v_{avg} \ge 1.8\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $v_{max} \le 3.6\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $v_{pp} \le 0.05\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $t_{up} \le 0.4\text{ s}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $dv \le 0.02\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
    *   Operating Conditions:
        *   S1: Nom (50uA, 100Hz, 25nF, 330k)
        *   S2: Heavy load (50uA, 100Hz, 25nF, 150k) -> FBR fails $v_{avg}$ and $t_{up}$.
        *   S3: Strong excitation, light load (100uA, 100Hz, 25nF, 2200k) -> FBR fails $v_{max}$ and $dv$.
        *   S4: Weak excitation (30uA, 100Hz, 25nF, 1000k) -> FBR fails $v_{avg}$ and $t_{up}$.
        *   S5: Low frequency (40uA, 80Hz, 25nF, 470k) -> FBR fails $dv$.
        *   S6: Hot, high Cp (50uA, 100Hz, 30nF, 330k) -> FBR ok.

    *   FBR (Full Bridge Rectifier) uses 4 diodes.
    *   $V_{OC, peak} = I_p / (2\pi f C_p)$. For nominal: $50\text{uA} / (2\pi \cdot 100 \cdot 25\text{nF}) \approx 3.18\text{ V}$.
    *   Since $V_{OC}$ is low, the $2 \times V_{diode}$ drop ($\approx 0.5\text{V}$ for DSCH) is significant.
    *   S3 (Strong excitation) causes $V_{out}$ to exceed $3.6\text{V}$.
    *   S2 and S4 (Heavy load/Weak excitation) don't reach $1.8\text{V}$ fast enough or at all.

    *   To improve efficiency and startup, we need something better than a passive bridge.
    *   SSHI (Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor) is the gold standard for piezos. It flips the voltage across $C_p$ at the peaks, effectively increasing the energy extracted per cycle.
    *   *Basic SSHI* (or Parallel-SSHI): An inductor $L$ is switched across the piezo terminals at the voltage extrema.
    *   *Circuit Topology for SSHI (with rectification):*
        1.  Piezo $\to$ Rectifier $\to$ $C_{out}$.
        2.  Inductor $L$ switched across the piezo terminals using a SYNC controller.
    *   Wait, the most common SSHI setup is to place the inductor in parallel with the piezo and switch it at the peaks, while a rectifier extracts the energy.

    *   *Topology 1: SSHI (Standard Parallel).*
        - Piezo terminals: `pzp`, `pzn`.
        - Full bridge rectifier: `pzp` $\to$ `D1` $\to$ `out`, `pzn` $\to$ `D2` $\to$ `out`, `0` $\to$ `D3` $\to$ `pzp`, `0` $\to$ `D4` $\to$ `pzn`.
        - Switchable inductor: `pzp` $\to$ `L1` $\to$ `S1` $\to$ `pzn`.
        - SYNC controller: `S1` closed at peaks (`edges: both`).
        - Storage: `Cout` at `out`.
        - Overvoltage protection: `DZ33` Zener at `out`.

    *   *Topology 2: Synchronous Rectifier (Active Bridge).*
        - Since we have limited components (16) and only 2 SYNCs, we can't make a full active bridge.
        - However, we can use a "Half-Bridge" or "Charge Pump" style.
        - Let's try a simpler "Buck-Boost" like approach or a "Synchronous Switching" approach to move charge more efficiently.
        - Actually, let's try a "Single-Ended SSHI" or a "Non-inverting" approach if possible.

    *   *Topology 3: SECE (Synchronized Electric Charge Extraction).*
        - The piezo charges a capacitor (via an inductor/switch), then that capacitor is dumped into the output.
        - This is usually more complex.

    *   **Proposal 1: Parallel SSHI**
        - Full bridge (4x DSCH) to `out`.
        - $L$ in parallel with piezo, switched by SYNC at both peaks.
        - $C_{out}$ for storage.
        - $DZ33$ Zener for $V_{max}$ limit (S3 fails $V_{max}$).
        - This should increase the average voltage $V_{out}$ and speed up $t_{up}$ by recovering energy from $C_p$.

    *   **Proposal 2: SSHI with a different rectifier (Half-Wave/Simplified)**
        - To save components or change the voltage level. But full bridge is more robust.
        - Let's try a "Boost" style: $L$ in series with a switch and diode.
        - Piezo $\to$ $L$ $\to$ $S$ $\to$ $D$ $\to$ $C_{out}$.
        - This might be too simple for a piezo.

    *   **Proposal 3: Improved FBR with Zener and larger capacitor**
        - The FBR failed S3 ($V_{max}$), S2 ($V_{avg}$), and S4 ($V_{avg}$).
        - A Zener `DZ33` fixes S3.
        - To fix S2/S4, we need more energy. SSHI is the way.
        - Let's try a variant of SSHI: "Series SSHI" (though Parallel is usually easier to implement with these components).

    - Piezo: `pzp`, `pzn`.
    - Full Bridge:
        - D1: `pzp` $\to$ `out` (DSCH)
        - D2: `pzn` $\to$ `out` (DSCH)
        - D3: `0` $\to$ `pzp` (DSCH)
        - D4: `0` $\to$ `pzn` (DSCH)
    - SSHI Path:
        - L1: `pzp` $\to$ `n1`
        - S1: `n1` $\to$ `pzn` (ctrl: G1)
        - G1: SYNC, `edges: both`, `ton` needs to be optimized ($\approx \pi \sqrt{L C_p}$), `phase: 0`.
    - Storage:
        - C1: `out` $\to$ `0`
    - Protection:
        - D5: `0` $\to$ `out` (DZ33)

    - Wait, check the components limit: 4 diodes (bridge) + 1 inductor + 1 switch + 1 SYNC + 1 cap (storage) + 1 Zener = 9 components. Well within 16.

    - $V_{max} \le 3.6\text{ V}$. DZ33 breaks down at 3.3V. This should keep $V_{out}$ under 3.6V (though the Zener current might increase).
    - $v_{avg} \ge 1.8\text{ V}$. SSHI increases the energy harvested by flipping $V_{Cp}$. This should help S2 and S4.
    - $v_{pp} \le 0.05\text{ V}$. $C_{out}$ should be large enough to filter.
    - $t_{up} \le 0.4\text{ s}$. SSHI's efficiency helps.
    - $dv \le 0.02\text{ V}$. Stable state.

    - $V_{out}$ is clamped at 3.3V.
    - $L$ is flipped at $V_{max}$ and $V_{min}$ of the piezo.
    - Does this meet all constraints? Let's check S3 again. S3 had $V_{out} = 5.7\text{V}$ with FBR. With DZ33, it will be $\approx 3.3\text{V}$, which is $\le 3.6\text{V}$.

    - Could we use a different inductor placement?
    - If we use a synchronous rectifier (using switches), we could reduce the 0.5V drop.
    - But we only have 2 SYNCs.
    - SYNC1 for the $L$-flip (SSHI), SYNC2 for... ?
    - We could use SYNC2 to switch the rectifier diodes. For example, a synchronous half-wave rectifier.
    - But a full bridge is very reliable. Let's stick to the Parallel SSHI.

    - Let's try a "Synchronous Boost" approach for the second proposal.
    - Piezo $\to$ L $\to$ S $\to$ C_out.
    - This is essentially what SSHI does but slightly different.
    - Actually, the "Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor" is specifically designed for piezo.
    - Let's try another variation: instead of a full bridge, use a center-tapped-like arrangement? (Not possible without a transformer).
    - Let's try a "Charge Pump" style for Proposal 2.
    - Or maybe just a different SSHI configuration?
    - No, Parallel SSHI is the most standard. Let's provide it as the main.

    - Let's consider a "Half-Bridge" for Proposal 2 to see if the reduced diode drop helps S2/S4.
    - Rectifier: D1 (`pzp` $\to$ `out`), D2 (`0` $\to$ `pzn`). (Wait, this only works for half a cycle).
    - Standard half-wave: D1 (`pzp` $\to$ `out`), $C_{out}$ to ground. (Wasteful).

    - Let's think about the "S2: heavy load" (150k). $P_{load} = V^2/R = 1.8^2/150\text{k} \approx 21.6\mu\text{W}$.
    - Piezo power: $P_{avg} = \frac{1}{2} I_p V_{OC} f \approx 0.5 \cdot 50\mu\text{A} \cdot 3.18\text{V} \cdot 100\text{Hz} \approx 79.5\mu\text{W}$.
    - FBR efficiency is low because $V_{OC}$ is only 3.2V, and $V_{out}$ is 1.8V.
    - SSHI should significantly boost this.

    - I'll propose:
        1. Parallel SSHI (Standard)
        2. Parallel SSHI with a slightly different rectifier (maybe just 2 diodes and a switch? No, let's try 3 diodes - "quasi-full-bridge").
        3. A "Modified FBR" with a Zener and a very large capacitor, just in case the SSHI is too aggressive (though unlikely).

    - Actually, let's refine Proposal 2: SSHI with a "Synchronous" switch for the output.
    - Instead of a diode to `out`, use a switch?
    - L1: `pzp` $\to$ `n1`, S1: `n1` $\to$ `pzn` (SYNC G1).
    - Rectifier: D1 (`pzp` $\to$ `out`), D2 (`pzn` $\to$ `out`), D3 (`0` $\to$ `pzp`), D4 (`0` $\to$ `pzn`).
    - This is already Proposal 1.

    - Let's try Proposal 2 as an "Inverting" SSHI? No.
    - Let's try a "C-SSH" (Capacitor-based SSHI) if possible? No, that needs more switches.

    - Let's go with:
        - Design 1: Parallel SSHI + Full Bridge + Zener.
        - Design 2: Parallel SSHI + Half Bridge (to see if lower diode drop on the main path helps) + Zener. (Wait, half bridge is worse).
        - Design 3: Parallel SSHI + Full Bridge (DSCH) + larger storage cap (no Zener, let's see if it's needed). No, S3 needs Zener.

    - Wait, "S3: strong excitation, light load" $V_{max}$ failed. $V_{OC, peak}$ for S3 is $100\mu\text{A} / (2\pi \cdot 100 \cdot 25\text{nF}) \approx 6.36\text{ V}$.
    - With FBR, $V_{out}$ can go up to $V_{OC} - 0.5\text{V} \approx 5.8\text{ V}$.
    - We *must* have a Zener `DZ33` to clamp it at 3.3V.

    - Let's stick to one very strong candidate: Parallel SSHI.
    - And a variation: SSHI where the inductor is switched using only one edge? (No, both is better).
    - How about a "Synchronous Rectifier" using the second SYNC?
    - SYNC 1: Inductor flip (both edges).
    - SYNC 2: Switch S2 closes when piezo voltage is high to bypass one diode?
    - That's getting complex. Let's just do:
        1. Parallel SSHI + Full Bridge + Zener.
        2. Parallel SSHI + Full Bridge (no Zener, but with a different $C_{out}$).
        3. Full Bridge + Zener + Large $C_{out}$ (to see if the Zener alone fixes FBR for S3, and if $C_{out}$ fixes S5).

    - Wait, the reference FBR failed S2 (heavy load) and S4 (weak excitation) on $v_{avg}$. Zener won't help that. Only SSHI or reduced diode drop will.

    - $L = 1\text{mH}$ to $10\text{mH}$.
    - $C_{out} = 1\mu\text{F}$ to $22\mu\text{F}$.
    - $t_{on} \approx \pi \sqrt{L C_p}$. For $L=1\text{mH}, C_p=25\text{nF}, t_{on} \approx 3.14 \cdot \sqrt{25\cdot 10^{-12}} \approx 15.7\mu\text{s}$.
    - These will be optimized.

    -- L1: `pzp` $\to$ `n1`
    - - S1: `n1` $\to$ `pzn`, ctrl: `G1`
    - - G1: SYNC, `edges: both`, `ton: 15u`, `phase: 0`
    - - D1: `pzp` $\to$ `out`, model: `DSCH`
    - - D2: `pzn` $\to$ `out`, model: `DSCH`
    - - D3: `0` $\to$ `pzp`, model: `DSCH`
    - - D4: `0` $\to$ `pzn`, model: `DSCH`
    - - D5: `0` $\to$ `out`, model: `DZ33`
    - - C1: `out` $\to$ `0`

    - Is this the best? The Zener `DZ33` clamps at 3.3V. $V_{max} \le 3.6\text{V}$ is ok. $V_{avg} \ge 1.8\text{V}$ is ok.
    - One detail: If $V_{out}$ reaches 3.3V, the diodes in the bridge start to be reverse-biased by the $V_{out}$ voltage.
    - $V_{pzp}$ must reach $V_{out} + 0.25\text{V} \approx 3.55\text{V}$ to conduct.
    - In S4, $V_{OC, peak} \approx 1.9\text{V}$. If $V_{out} = 1.8\text{V}$, $V_{pzp}$ must be $2.05\text{V}$. SSHI helps increase $V_{pzp}$.

    - *Wait!* There's a simpler way to do SSHI: use the inductor to flip the voltage, but we can also use a "synchronous" switch to charge the capacitor.
    - Let's just provide the Parallel SSHI. It's the most robust.

    - Proposals:
        1. `sshi_fbr`: Parallel SSHI + Full Bridge + Zener.
        2. `sshi_hb`: Parallel SSHI + Half Bridge (S1 switches, etc.) - No, let's try `sshi_fbr_no_zener` to see if the optimizer finds a better $C_{out}$ that doesn't need clamping (unlikely for S3).
        3. `fbr_zener`: FBR + Zener + large $C_{out}$. (Simple baseline).

    - Actually, the prompt says "up to 3 designs". I'll provide the SSHI and a couple of variations.

    - Components:
        - L1: `pzp`, `n1`
        - S1: `n1`, `pzn`, ctrl: `G1`
        - G1: SYNC
        - D1: `pzp`, `out`
        - D2: `pzn`, `out`
        - D3: `0`, `pzp`
        - D4: `0`, `pzn`
        - D5: `0`, `out` (DZ33)
        - C1: `out`, `0`
    - Total components: 9. (Under 16).
